sections.content: Columns, left to right: (select box), #, Quotation No, BL Ref No, Shipper, Consignee, Vessel, Voyage, Leg, ETA, Main Line, Vessel Operator, POL, POD, Transhipment Port, Equipment Type, Qty, BL Creation, F / E, ACID Check, Status, D.O, Attach, Actions ETA prints as dd-mm-yyyy, or "-" when the voyage has no ETA row for that port. BL Creation prints the full date and time. "Attach" is the DOCUMENTS menu (the bars icon) — not the file attachments. Attachments are a separate red PDF button in the Actions column, shown only when the BL has attachments; it opens all of them merged into one PDF. Equipment Type is a link; it opens an Equipment Summary popup with the per-type counts, total containers and total TEUs for that BL. Selecting rows: Each row has a tick box, and the header tick box selects the page. Selecting the header box also offers "select every BL matching the current filters, across all pages". While anything is selected, the ACTIONS column header swaps from the word "Actions" to two buttons: Check ACI for Selected (only when the ACI flag is on) Delete Selected (see section 6) Selections survive paging (kept per session) until cleared. Header widget (all filtered rows, not just the current page): Total Bookings / Total Containers / Total TEUs Cancelled BLs are left out of those totals. The same physical container counted on more than one BL is counted once. Filters (can be combined): Quotation No One quotation, or the special "No Quotation" option (quotation_id = 0). Import BL REF NO BL number. BL Status Confirm / Draft / Cancelled. Created by User who created the BL (booked_by). Shipper Import shippers. Freight Forwarder Consignee DO Printed Yes = at least one row in do_prints for this BL. No = never recorded as printed. This is the do_prints table, not the print_count number. See 02. Direct / Transhipment shipment_type_filter. POL / POD Vessel / Voyage Multi-select of voyage IDs. Matches voyage_id OR voyage_id_second. Cross switch Next to Vessel / Voyage. Only becomes active when a voyage is also selected. Then the list includes sibling companies that share the same company CODE as the logged-in company, matching the same voyage_no + serial. The voyage dropdown itself still shows only THIS company's voyages. Type IMO or OOG (cargo_type) — BLs that have at least one such container line. Container No ETA From / ETA To

sections.heading: Creating & Editing
sections.content: Manual create rules (Import): Discharge port is required and must differ from load port. Error: "Load Port The Same Discharge Port" UCR, if typed, must be exactly 19 digits. Error: "UCR must be exactly 19 digits." Container numbers on the same BL must be unique. Error: "Container Numbers must be unique" If a BL ref is typed, it must be unique in the company. Error: "This Booking No Already Exists" For Sobek only: every container number must already exist in the line-visible container master. Error: "Container No: {value} is not Found." Missing containers are created for non-Sobek Import (number + type from the form). do_hold can be ticked on create/edit. Edit uses booking.edit when a quotation exists, otherwise booking.noquotation.edit. A short Edit Summary path exists for a limited field set. Five Excel uploads sit on this same screen (Upload dropdown). Templates are in the Templates dropdown. BL Header Creates BL header rows only (BookingImport). Template: documents/summary_booking_template.xlsx Route: importBooking Duplicate ref in the same company is rejected. BL Details Adds container lines onto an EXISTING BL (BookingDetailsImport). Template: documents/booking_import_template.xlsx Route: importBookingDetails Looks up the BL by booking_no in this company. Discharge List Container + booking import (ContainerBookingImport). Template: documents/discharge_list_template.xls Route: booking.container-import Manifest List Older / shorter ship-manifest upload (ManifestImport). Template: documents/manifest_import_template.xlsx Route: importShipManifest Creates Import BLs from a simpler Excel than EDI. EDI Manifest Full create path: vessel header + one row per container, creates Confirm Import BLs, customers, containers, and container lines in one file. Template: documents/edi_manifest_import_template.xlsx Route: invoice.importExtendedManifest Importer: ManifestExtendedImport See 03-edi-manifest-import.txt for every column, every reject reason, and transhipment/transit mapping. All uploads accept .xls / .xlsx (EDI also accepts .csv on the file picker). Failed rows produce a downloadable error Excel rather than a silent skip. Other list actions (not create): Check ACI for selected rows (only if the ACI flag is on). Delete Selected (section 6). Edit — the pencil on every row, opens in a new tab. Merge and Clone: the buttons are currently commented out of the list, so they cannot be reached from this screen even though the merge popup, the merge route and the "Merged BLs" / "Merged" statuses all still exist. Rows that were merged in the past still display those statuses. Merge sets the parent to status 4 and each child to status 5. Part Load / Rollover / Transhipment assign / WTOR — handled by this controller but not by a button on this list. 5b. EXPORTS AND BULK PRINTS FROM THE TOOLBAR Export dropdown behaviour is not uniform: BL List / Discharge List / Transhipment List / DO Prints / Seals List Submit the CURRENT filter form. No row selection needed; what you filtered is what you get. Manifest List Works on SELECTED rows only (or on select-all). With nothing selected it refuses: "No Selection - Please select at least one BL draft to export." Print dropdown (Print Manifests / DGD Report / Shipment Statement) also uses the current filters, and explicitly sends cross=0 when the Cross switch is off.

sections.heading: Deleting
sections.content: There is NO delete button on an individual row of this list. The only way to delete from this screen is: tick one or more rows (or select all pages), then press the trash button that appears in the Actions column header. Confirmation text: "{n} selected booking(s) will be permanently deleted! This cannot be undone." Select-all mode instead warns: "ALL {n} booking(s) matching the current filters (all pages) will be permanently deleted! This cannot be undone." Bulk delete skips (does not delete) a BL when: 1. It has any invoice — either directly on booking_ref, or through an Export BL draft linked to it. 2. It has any movement record. Skipped BLs are named back to the user: "{n} booking(s) deleted successfully. The following {n} booking(s) could not be deleted because they have invoices or related movements: {refs}" If nothing could be deleted: "The following booking(s) cannot be deleted because they have invoices or related movements: {refs}" If nothing matched at all: "No bookings were found or accessible." Deleted BLs lose their container IMO sub-lines and container lines first, then the BL row itself. The whole batch runs in one transaction. The single-booking delete route (used from other screens) has a different, stricter set of guards: movements → "Cannot delete this booking. It has related movement records." has_bl → "Can't delete this booking. It has BL." invoices → "Can't delete this booking. It has related invoices."

sections.heading: How This Feeds Other Modules
sections.content: Priority of consumers (what looks this list up): 1. Movements Discharge / gate / WTOR are posted against this BL's containers and voyage. "All containers discharged" on the list is true only when every assigned container has a discharge movement (DCHF / DCHE / DITR / DCHT) on this BL or on the BL's voyage / second voyage. Sobek is treated as already discharged *. A BL with no assigned container_ids is also treated as discharged. This gate feeds DO, Release Order, and Import invoice confirm. 2. Invoices / Debits / Credit notes Created against booking_ref = this BL. Confirmed unpaid invoices (and, on the list, unpaid debits that are not fully credited) block Release Order for non-credit customers. Any invoice at all blocks delete. 3. Detention / Storage / Power Use this BL's containers, voyage ETD/ETA, and free_time from the container line (EDI "NO. FREE DEMURRAGE DAYS"). 4. CUSCAR / Nafeza / ACI ACID, importer/exportal tax, consignee code, and ports on this BL are what customs messages send. Failed ACI shows on the list; it does not by itself hide documents. 5. Arrival Notification PDF always from the documents menu (when the menu is unlocked). and you can send it by Email. 6. Release Order / Gate letters Party = receiver if named, else consignee. Credit flag on that party skips payment/free-day checks. 7. DO Print Counter / do_prints See 02-do-print-counter.txt. The DO Printed filter on THIS screen reads do_prints. 8. DOCUMENTS OPENED FROM THIS LIST (where, not the DO counter) Two columns sit after Status: D.O Delivery Order only. Full rules in 02-do-print-counter.txt. Attach (documents menu) Shown only when status is Confirm (1) or Merged-parent (4). If do_hold is on, the whole menu is replaced by a red lock ("DO On Hold - documents cannot be printed"). When the menu is open, items are: Cargo Manifest Always (for an unlocked Confirm/Merged-parent row). PDF: booking.showImportManifestPDF Cargo Manifest Excel Always. Route: manifest.excel Gate In / Civil Defense / VGM Letter Hidden when the BL is a Transhipment-in-Egypt booking UNLESS at least one container line is IMO. Gate In opens a terminal/depot picker first. SOC Letter Same transhipment/IMO hide rule as Gate In, AND at least one container must be SOC (line soc = 1 or the container master SOC_COC = SOC). Release Order Same transhipment/IMO hide rule as Gate In. Stops: Stop 1: not all containers discharged "Not all containers have been Discharged" Stop 2: party is a credit customer → allowed Stop 3: unpaid invoice/debit (not void, not marked paid, not fully credited) "Has unpaid invoices — please settle outstanding charges first" Stop 4: no confirmed invoice yet AND free days have expired (voyage discharge ETD + 4 days to end of that day; if no ETD, free days are treated as still open) "Free storage period has expired — please settle charges first" Otherwise a trucker modal opens, then Containerized or Non-Containerized Release Letter. Arrival Notification (PDF)/Email Always on an unlocked Confirm/Merged-parent row. Edit Report Only if an edit-track row exists for the BL. Draft, Cancelled, and Merged-child rows do not get the D.O icon or the documents menu.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Every Import invoice, discharge movement, Release Order, and customs ACID check points at a row on this list. The most common operational mistake is treating EDI Manifest as a "just upload" step: a wrong voyage, a POD/FPOD pair that flips the BL into transhipment/transit, or a Company Code that is not the logged-in company, drops that BL from the file (error Excel) or creates it on the wrong voyage. The second most common mistake is expecting DO / Release Order to print before every container has a discharge movement, or while DO Hold is ticked on the edit form.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: A Delivery Order (DO) tells the terminal the cargo may be delivered. This screen sets how many times a BL may be printed and lets you clear a print so it can be printed again. Two counters exist and they are not the same thing: Print count / Max print Numbers on the BL. The D.O cell shows them as "print count / max print" and goes grey when the count has reached the max. Printed / Unprinted Whether a real (non-draft) DO has been printed. This is what the Import list filter "DO Printed" uses, and what turns the MLHE / MLHC / NMD menu item from Print into Printed. Resetting "Printed" does not zero the print count, and editing the print count does not clear "Printed". A BL can show Printed while its count is still 0, or the reverse.

sections.heading: The Counter Screen
sections.content: The screen is empty until you search. Search "Search by Booking Ref No" Partial match on the BL number. Each hit shows the print count, the max, and a Printed or Unprinted badge. Print Counter / Max Print, then Save Both numbers are saved exactly as typed. A BL's max may be higher or lower than the global number. Printed badge Click it to reset. Every print record for that BL is deleted. "Reset {ref}: removed {n} print record(s). You can now reprint the DO." The print count is NOT cleared. If the count is already at the max, zero it (or raise the max) as well, or Print stays blocked. Unprinted Nothing to reset. Max Print Number (top left) → Update Required whole number, 0 or more. Writes that max onto every BL whose max is empty or lower than or equal to the new number. BLs that already have a HIGHER max are left alone. "Global max print count updated successfully. Updated {n} booking(s) to {value}." If any were kept: "{n} booking(s) with higher custom values were preserved." There is no separate delete. Reset is the only way to remove print records. The BL itself is not deleted. What a print writes: MLHE / MLHC / NMD: a real Print adds a Printed record and does not increase the print count. Draft writes nothing. The stops in section 5 are enforced on the list. The PDF address itself does not re-check them, so opening a saved link still produces the file and, for a real DO, still counts as a print.

sections.heading: What Stops Each Document
sections.content: First failing stop wins. These are on Import BL List. SHARED — D.O column and the Attach menu 1. Status is not Confirm and not "Confirm + Merged BLs". Draft, Cancelled, and a BL that was merged into another one: no D.O icon and no Attach menu. 2. DO Hold is ticked on the BL. D.O shows a lock. Attach is replaced by a red lock: "DO On Hold - documents cannot be printed". "Discharged" means every container on the BL has a discharge movement (DCHF, DCHE, DITR or DCHT), either on this BL or on its voyage / second voyage. A BL with no containers assigned counts as discharged. Sobek is always treated as discharged. TRANSHIPMENT MENU When the BL tranships IN Egypt (Egypt is the transhipment port, not the final POD), Gate In, Civil Defense, VGM Letter, SOC Letter and Release Order all disappear together — unless at least one container is IMO. The menu then only has Cargo Manifest, Cargo Manifest Excel, Arrival Notification, and Edit Report if the BL was edited. That is normal. DELIVERY ORDER Where: column "D.O". The counter screen does not print a PDF; it only changes the limits. Only company codes MLHE, MLHC and NMD can print a DO from this list. Any other company code leaves the icon disabled. For those three companies, in order: DO Hold → red lock, "DO On Hold" Not discharged → blue anchor, "Awaiting Discharge" Otherwise a menu: Draft does not count as a print. Watermarked, labelled DRAFT.{id} Print real Original + Copy. Confirm popup: "This is a one-time action. Once printed, the Print option will be permanently disabled for this BL." Printed Print is disabled, "Already printed" Print is also disabled when the print count has reached the max, even if hold is off and the cargo is discharged: "Cannot print DO - check hold status, invoices and payment" The cell is grey and shows count/max underneath. Voyage printed on the DO: second voyage when the BL is flagged transhipment, otherwise the first voyage, at the discharge port. CARGO MANIFEST (PDF and Excel) Where: Attach menu. Stops: the two shared stops only. The PDF leaves out Summary Booking rows. Containers that do not fit the first page continue on extra sheets. Print Manifests (top Print dropdown) is the same document for many BLs: it uses the current filters, including Cross, and does not check hold, discharge or the print counter per row. GATE IN Where: Attach menu → Gate In popup. Terminal/Depot is required (Egypt terminals, shown as "Port - CODE"). No terminal, no PDF. Stops: shared stops, plus the transhipment menu rule. CIVIL DEFENSE Where: Attach menu. No popup. Stops: shared stops, plus the transhipment menu rule. VGM LETTER (خطاب وزن حاوية) Where: Attach menu → popup. Terminal/Depot is required. Trucker is optional. "الخط الملاحي (Shipping line)" appears only for agency MLH and NMD. Stops: shared stops, plus the transhipment menu rule. A container numbered "000" is left off the letter. SOC LETTER (خطاب SOC) Where: Attach menu → popup. Hidden completely when no container is SOC (the container line is marked SOC, or the container master says SOC). Addressee (Terminal/Depot) is optional. Leave it on "-- Use booking terminal --" to use the BL's terminal. Stops: shared stops, plus the transhipment menu rule. The letter only lists SOC containers, and only those with a real container number (not blank, not "000"). If the SOC mark is missing on both the line and the container, the letter opens with an empty table. RELEASE ORDER (Release Letter) Where: Attach menu → "Release Letter - Select Trucker". Two buttons: Containerized Release Letter, and Non-Containerized Release Letter. Trucker is optional. Stops, in order: Shared stops (status, DO Hold) Transhipment-in-Egypt menu rule (hidden, unless IMO) Not discharged "Not all containers have been Discharged" The receiver (or the consignee, if no receiver is named) is a credit customer → allowed, money checks skipped An invoice or a debit is still unpaid (not void, not marked paid, and not fully covered by a credit note) "Has unpaid invoices — please settle outstanding charges first" There is no confirmed invoice yet AND the free days have run out Free days = the discharge-port voyage ETD plus 4 days, through the end of that last day. No ETD on the voyage → treated as still free. "Free storage period has expired — please settle charges first" Containers with no real number, or number "000", are left off the letter. The storage date printed on it is the end date of the latest Storage (or Extension Storage) invoice; if there is none, it is worked out from the voyage ETA and the storage tariff. Choosing a trucker can be blocked on its own (MLH). These do not disable the PDF button; they stop a new trucker being picked: "Equipment Type Price Missing" No trucking price for this BL's equipment, so no new trucker can be assigned. A trucker already on the BL stays. "Insufficient Balance" Shows what is available, the shortfall and the balance afterwards. Cancel restores the previous trucker. Confirm keeps the choice; the balance is applied when the container's WTOR or gate-out movement is recorded. "This trucker has no guarantee yet." Asks for Valid From and Valid To. Both are required: "Please enter both Valid From and Valid To." Closing it without saving undoes the trucker pick. Generating the letter saves the chosen trucker on the BL. For MLHE, MLHC and NMD it also creates WTOR movements for the containers, silently, and does not duplicate ones that already exist. ARRIVAL NOTIFICATION (PDF) Where: Attach menu. Stops: the two shared stops only. Uses the second voyage when the BL is transhipment, otherwise the first, at the discharge port. ARRIVAL NOTIFICATION (EMAIL) Where: Attach menu. Shown only when the agency is MSL. Stops: shared stops, plus that MSL-only rule. Needs a valid recipient address and a subject. A bad CC address stops the send: "Some CC emails are invalid: {list}" Default CC addresses are added automatically. It can be resent; the BL remembers who sent it and when. EDIT REPORT Where: Attach menu. Shown only when the BL has edit history. Stops: shared stops. No history → the item is absent. DGD REPORT Where: top Print dropdown. Uses the current filters. Does not check hold, discharge or the print counter. Only IMO containers are included, so the report can be empty even when BLs matched. No BL matched the filters: "No bookings found with the selected filters." SHIPMENT STATEMENT Where: top Print dropdown. Same filters, same empty message, and the same lack of hold / discharge / print-counter checks.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: A print count already at the max (including a max left at 0) blocks the DO even when the cargo is discharged and hold is off. After one real print on MLHE / MLHC / NMD, Print stays disabled until Printed is reset on this screen — and that reset does not lower the print count, so both have to be checked. The usual reason NOTHING on the row will print, DO included, is DO Hold on the BL edit form.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: EDI Manifest is the bulk way to CREATE Confirm Import BLs from a line / agent Excel. One file carries the vessel/voyage once, then one data row per container (several rows may share the same BL number). The importer creates the BL header, finds or creates shipper / consignee / notify, finds or creates containers, and writes every container line (hazmat, OOG, reefer, SOC/COC, freight). It does not update an existing BL. If the BL number already exists in that company, that BL is rejected and later BLs in the file still continue.

sections.heading: What Each BL Becomes in the System
sections.content: Every accepted BL is created as: shipment_type Import booking_confirm 1 (Confirm) — never Draft movement FCL/FCL payment_kind Collect(THC) f_kind Prepaid if AD=P, Collect if AD=C (FREIGHT) booking_type FULL/EMPTY column (lowercased) ref_no column A commodity all J texts for that BL + HTS from K acid AQ exportal_id AR (shipper tax) importer_id AS (consignee tax) principal_name line found from row-2 LINE NAME booked_by the user who uploaded vessel_name the found vessel id loading_date AW converted to a date pod_collection BB if numeric(used to OWNER account inv.) Parties (find-or-create): Shipper from B + C, tax from AR. Country set from AT (exporter prefix) when that code exists. Consignee from E + F + D (consignee code), tax from AS. Country forced to Egypt (EG) unless the consignee code is the word "bank". Notify from G + H. Customer matching is a chain, not a simple lookup, and it searches the WHOLE customer master (it is not limited to your own company's customers): 1. Exact name match. 2. Exact tax-number match. 3. If both exist but point at DIFFERENT customers: - the name-matched customer has no tax yet → the sheet's tax is written onto it; - otherwise the BL is rejected: "Customer name '{name}' matches '{db name}' (tax: {tax}), but tax number '{tax}' is already assigned to '{other}'. Please reconcile the customer master data or the Excel sheet." 4. Name match only → the tax must agree, else: "Customer '{name}' already exists in the system with tax number '{tax}', but the Excel sheet provides a different tax number '{tax}'..." A customer with an empty tax gets the sheet's tax written onto it (and is marked as a tax customer). 5. Tax match only → the name must be the same or at least 75% similar, else: "Tax number '{tax}' is already assigned to customer '{name}' in the system, but the Excel sheet provides a different customer name '{name}'..." 6. Creating a brand new customer also refuses to reuse a tax already held by someone else: "Tax number '{tax}' is already assigned to customer '{name}' in the system." 7. No exact match at all → fuzzy name matching, with deliberately different strictness: Shipper and Notify are treated as CRITICAL: - if the sheet gives a tax number and nothing matched exactly, fuzzy matching is SKIPPED and a new customer is created; - with no tax number, the name must be 90% similar (and, when an address is given, the address at least 70% similar). Consignee and everything else: 75% name similarity, plus 70% address similarity when an address is supplied. A fuzzy hit reuses the existing customer under its OLD name; the Excel spelling is not saved. 8. Still nothing → a new customer is created with name and code both set to the Excel name, the address, and the tax number. Every resolved customer gets the matching role (Shipper / Consignee / Notify) attached if it does not have it. Bank consignees: when the consignee code is "bank" or "999999999", the row is treated as a bank. Tax checks are skipped (banks may share tax numbers), a Consignee Bank record is created or reused, linked to the customer, and that bank record — not a normal customer — becomes the BL's consignee. Ports: POL = column I (must exist). POD / FPOD = AU / AV. If a cell is empty the vessel-block POD is used as fallback for the discharge port. POD vs FPOD decides the routing flag (see section 5). Containers: Number L, type M, ISO N, line code O, seal P, packages Q, pack type R, weight S, tare T, DG U/V/AF, temps W/X/Y, OOG Z + AL..AP, freight AA/AB/AC, free days AG, SOC/COC AI (0=COC 1=SOC), part load AJ, reefer AK, operator AY. Containers are GLOBAL master data — they are looked up by container number only, with no company filter. Equipment type is resolved by matching the type name (M) OR the ISO code (N) against Equipment Types. If the container number already EXISTS: It is reused as-is. Its type, tare weight and SOC/COC are NOT updated from the sheet, even when the Excel values differ — the update statement is deliberately switched off in the code. Only the operator-code check runs: if the stored operator code differs from AY, the BL still imports and an operator-code alert is recorded against the voyage for review. If the container number is NEW: It is created with the resolved type, the tare, the SOC/COC value (defaulting to COC), stock status "not in stock", and operator code AY — falling back to the container line code (O) when AY is empty. Seal defaults to "NA" when P is blank. Temperature unit defaults to C. Watch out: the importer checks that column M is filled, but not that the type actually exists. An unknown type does not produce the clean "Container Type '{name}' not found in database" message — the BL fails later with a technical error in the report instead. Treat any odd technical message on a BL as "check the equipment type and ISO code first". Dangerous goods (DG): UN NO (V) may hold several UN numbers separated by commas. Each is padded to four digits (7 becomes 0007) and looked up in the system's UN dangerous-goods list. IMO CLASS (U) is taken per UN number from the sheet when given, otherwise from that list. Proper shipping name (AF) is only auto-filled from the list when the sheet leaves it blank; several names are joined with " // " and UN numbers with " , ". A container counts as IMO when a class was resolved. Description of goods: Column J is collected from every row of the BL, blanks and exact duplicates are dropped, and what is left is joined with line breaks into the BL's commodity description. A BL therefore only gets a description from rows that also carry a container number. Same container number twice on the SAME BL: One merged container line (packs and weights summed, is_sub_imo = true) plus one IMO-sub row per Excel line. That is how multi-commodity / multi-UN boxes are stored. BL number starting with "/": Treated as a child of the parent without the slash (parent_id set if that parent already exists). If the parent is imported later in the same file, children that were waiting get parent_id filled. total_gross_weight on the BL = sum of S for all its rows.

sections.heading: Transhipment / Transit Written by the File
sections.content: Compared after ports are resolved (codes or names). AU POD equals AV FPOD (example: EGALY / EGALY) Direct Import. voyage_id = the found voyage. discharge_port = POD. No transhipment port. is_transhipment = 0. AU POD differs from AV FPOD transhipment_port is set to the original POD. discharge_port becomes FPOD. Then: If original POD country is Egypt is_transhipment = 1 voyage_id = the found voyage This is "tranship in Egypt, final elsewhere". If original POD country is NOT Egypt voyage_id is left empty voyage_id_second = the found voyage is_transhipment stays 0 This is the file's "transit" case (foreign tranship, final POD from FPOD). Per-BL terminal (AX) overrides row-2 POD TERMINAL when filled. Exporter country (AT) and ACID (AQ) are NOT required when POD differs from FPOD (the file treats that as transhipment for validation). They ARE required when FULL/EMPTY is "full" and POD equals FPOD. 6. VALIDATION (what stops a BL — not the whole file) The file is processed BL by BL. A failed BL is skipped; others continue. Failed BLs and their containers are counted as not imported and written to an error Excel. Vessel-level (stops the entire file): Missing Vessel Name / Call Sign / Voyage Number / Port of Discharge / POD Terminal. Per-BL rejects (verbatim / near-verbatim messages): "BL number is missing in row {n}" Column A empty. "Line Code and Company Code are required" AZ or BA empty. "You can only upload data to your company ({CODE})" BA company code must match the logged-in company's code (case-insensitive). Example file BA=MLHE only works when the user is an MLHE company. If you are switched to another line (page-title line switcher), the whole file is rejected BL by BL with this message — switch line first, then upload. "Company with Line Code '{AZ}' and Company Code '{BA}' not found in database" No company has that line code together with that value as EITHER its company code or its agency code. Required header fields (empty → "Required field missing: {name}"): BL Number, Shipper, Shipper Address, Consignee, Port of Loading, Description of Goods, Line Code, Company Code. Description of Goods is built from column J on rows that also have a container number — a BL with no container row will fail this. "Consignee Code is required" Column D empty. Exporter Country Code Required when NOT (POD!=FPOD) AND FULL/EMPTY is full. ACID when FULL/EMPTY is full AND POD equals FPOD: "ACID is required when booking type is 'full'" "ACID must be exactly 19 characters long when booking type is 'full' (provided: {n})" Example file AQ=7721397921022910018 (19 chars). "At least one container is required" Per container: Container Number, Container Type, Packing Type required. Number of Packages and Gross Weight required and must be greater than 0 — except packages are skipped when FULL/EMPTY is empty. "Container {no}: {field} is required" "Container {no}: {field} is required and must be greater than 0" "BL number {ref} already exists" Same ref_no already in that company (all companies checked, not only the current scope). Port / terminal / vessel / voyage / principal / country lookup failures use the "not found in database" messages in section 3. Customer / tax clashes: The four messages listed in section 4. Any of them rejects that BL only. 6b. WHAT THE SYSTEM TELLS YOU AFTERWARDS Everything clean: "All {n} bls were imported successfully! {n} containers imported." Some BLs failed: "Import completed with {n} errors. {n} bls were imported successfully. {n} containers imported, {n} containers not imported." plus a link to a downloadable error workbook. Vessel row invalid (nothing was imported at all): "Import failed: Vessel data validation errors found. Please check the error report." Unexpected failure of the whole file: "Import failed: {technical message}" The error workbook has one line per problem, carrying the BL number, the error message, and the vessel, voyage, POL, POD, shipper, consignee, line code and company code for that BL so the file can be corrected without hunting for the row. The same message on the same BL is listed once, so one BL with three different problems gives three lines. "Containers not imported" counts the container rows of every REJECTED BL, not individual bad containers — one rejected BL with ten boxes adds ten to that number.

sections.heading: How This Feeds Import BL List and Downstream
items: 1. Import BL List The new rows appear as Confirm Import BLs. Voyage / ETA columns follow the list rules in 01-import-bl.txt (Egypt POD vs transhipment port). A file that sets POD != FPOD will show Transhipment port and may swap which voyage column is used.

2. Customers master New shipper / consignee / notify rows are created when no close name match exists (similarity ~75%, address ~70% when an address is present). Wrong spelling therefore creates a duplicate customer that invoices and Release Order will use.
3. Containers master Missing numbers are created with type, ISO, tare, SOC/COC, operator, line code. Existing numbers keep their old type.

4. Movements / DO / Release Order EDI does not write movements. DO and Release Order stay blocked until discharge is posted (see 02). Free demurrage days (AG) become container-line free_time for later detention.

5. Invoices / ACI / CUSCAR ACID, tax numbers, consignee code, ports, and commodity on the created BL are what customs and invoice screens read. payment_kind is Collect even when AD is Prepaid; only f_kind stores P/C.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: EDI Manifest is the fastest way to load a whole vessel, and the fastest way to load it wrong. The file never creates a voyage or a terminal — those names/codes must already match Voyage List and Terminals exactly (example: voyage 26LVX20 on vessel ARCHERFISH, terminal ACHCO at EGALY). Company code in column BA must be the logged-in company or every BL is rejected. POD versus FPOD silently flips the BL into transhipment/transit, which then changes the ETA column, the second voyage, and which letters hide on the Attach menu. A duplicate BL number is skipped, not updated, so a corrected EDI file will not repair a BL that already imported.

modules.title: Rollover
modules.summary: Rollover moves cargo that was planned on one sailing onto a later (or different) sailing when the original voyage is missed, delayed, or no longer suitable.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: Rollover moves cargo that was planned on one sailing onto a later (or different) sailing when the original voyage is missed, delayed, or no longer suitable. Export Booking supports two business shapes of rollover: A) Whole-booking rollover (by voyage) Keep the same booking number(s). Change the voyage on one or many bookings that currently sit on a selected sailing. Record where they came from (Roll From). Update related draft B/Ls and container movements so yard / ops stay aligned with the new sailing. B) Partial-container rollover (split booking) Keep some containers on the original booking / voyage. Move the selected containers onto a NEW booking with a new reference ending in R1, R2, ... on the destination voyage. Retarget those containers' movements to the new booking and voyage. Confirmed Bills of Lading must not be silently moved off their sailing. A booking with a Confirmed B/L is blocked from rollover.

steps.title: Open Rollover
steps.desc: Sidebar → Documentation → Export Booking.

steps.title: Search & Locate
steps.desc: A) Whole-booking (by voyage) Filter Export Booking to exactly one Vessel / Voyage

steps.title: Enter Details & Save
steps.desc: Click the Voyage column "Rollover" button → Choose the new voyage → Tick the eligible bookings (search by booking no if needed) → Confirm Rollover → Bookings stay on the same refs but now show the new voyage; Roll Fro…

steps.title: System Validates
steps.desc: Required fields, guards, and business rules are enforced before save.

steps.title: Ready in System
outcomes: A new booking appears as <original ref>R1 (or R2...) on the new voyage; remaining containers stay on the original booking.
Downstream screens can consume the updated data

sections.heading: What Each Mode Changes
items: Field / object Whole-booking rollover Partial-container Booking ref_no Unchanged New booking = original + R1/R2...
voyage_id Set to new voyage New booking gets new voyage; original keeps old
roll_from Set to previous Not set on the voyage_id new booking by this flow
Containers Stay on same booking Selected detail rows move to the new booking
total_quantity Unchanged by this flow Original = remaining rows; new = count moved
Draft B/L voyage_id Updated to new voyage Not cloned / (non-confirmed only) not moved here
Confirmed B/L Blocks the booking Row action hidden from selection when has_bl = 1
Movements (Export) Same booking_no; Moved containers: voyage + vessel updated; booking_no → new remark appended booking; voyage + vessel updated; remark appended

sections.heading: Entry Conditions & Eligibility
sections.content: A) Voyage "Rollover" button (list header) Shown only when the list filter has exactly one voyage selected. Otherwise the normal "Vessel / Voyage" header label is shown. If the user clicks without a single voyage selected, the system warns: "Please select exactly one voyage to perform rollover." Bookings offered for that voyage (same company, Export): - Status in Confirmed / Draft / related open statuses used by the list endpoint - Shown with container summary and B/L draft counts - can_rollover = false when any Confirmed B/L exists on the booking (row marked and checkbox replaced with a red block icon: "Cannot rollover - Confirmed B/L") - Draft B/L is allowed (row may be highlighted as a warning, but still selectable) Submit only updates bookings that: - Belong to the company - Are still on the current voyage set - Are Export - Have no Confirmed B/L - Were checked by the user - New voyage is different from current voyage If none remain eligible after those checks: "No eligible bookings found for rollover. Bookings with B/L cannot be rolled over." B) Per-row container Rollover icon Shown when ALL of the following are true on that row: - Booking status is Confirmed (or the "merged/confirmed" status used as 4 in the list) - Booking has_bl = 0 (no B/L created yet) - Total container qty on the booking is greater than 1 - At least one container is Assigned (Assigned = qty 1 with a real container number; empty / "000" slots count as Unassigned) Submit rules on the container screen: - New voyage is required and must not be the booking's current voyage (current voyage is excluded from the dropdown) - At least one container must be selected - Selected containers must belong to this booking - Cannot move ALL containers — at least one must remain: "Cannot rollover all containers. At least one container must remain in the original booking." - Unauthorized company access is rejected

sections.heading: New Booking Number
items: Pattern: <original_ref_no>R1 then R2, R3, ... if earlier rollover bookings already exist for that base ref in the same company
Example: MLHALYLTK08261261 original MLHALYLTK08261261R1 first partial rollover MLHALYLTK08261261R2 second partial rollover from the same base

The new booking copies commercial / route / party fields from the original (shipper, consignee, ports, quotation link, commodity, status, etc.) and sets total_quantity to the number of containers moved.

sections.heading: How This Feeds Movements & B/L
items: Priority of effects after a successful rollover:
1. Booking voyage Ops and Documentation lists now show the cargo under the new sailing. Whole-booking mode also stores Roll From so exports / reports can show the previous voyage number.

2. Draft B/L (whole-booking mode only) Non-confirmed draft B/Ls on the rolled bookings get the new voyage_id so print / Nafeza draft data match the new sailing. Confirmed B/Ls are never updated — those bookings were blocked.

3. Container movements (Export bookings only) Matching movement rows for the booking(s) (and, in partial mode, only the moved container ids) are updated to: - new voyage_id - new vessel_id from that voyage - optional new booking_no (partial mode) - remark text appended, e.g. "Rollover changed voyage from VESSEL / 26ABC to VESSEL / 26XYZ."
Import movements and non-export bookings are outside this update helper's scope.

4. Downstream consumers Anything that keys off booking.voyage_id, draft BL voyage, or movement voyage (equipment dashboards, sailing reports, yard sequences, export Excel "Roll From" column) will follow the new sailing after refresh. A Confirmed B/L left behind on the old sailing is exactly why Confirmed B/L blocks rollover.

sections.heading: Typical Success Messages
items: Whole-booking: "Successfully rolled over N selected booking(s) from 'OLD' to 'NEW'." Optionally appends movement and draft B/L update counts.
Partial-container: "Successfully rolled over N container(s) from <old ref> to <new ref>. New voyage: <vessel> / <voyage_no>" Optionally appends movement update count.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Without rollover, cargo that misses a cut-off stays booked on a sailing that will not carry it — wrong voyage on the booking, wrong draft B/L voyage, and movements that still point at the old vessel. Ops then gate out / load against inconsistent data. The Confirmed B/L hard stop exists so a released / confirmed bill is not quietly moved to another sailing while the paper / customs document still describes the old one. If cargo with a Confirmed B/L must change sailing, the B/L process must be handled first; do not expect Rollover to override it. The most common mistake on partial rollover is trying to move every container: the system refuses that so the original booking is never left empty by this path — use whole-booking rollover when the entire booking should change voyage under the same reference.

modules.title: Import CUSCAR
modules.summary: Generates the EDIFACT CUSCAR D.95B customs manifest required by NAFEZA for cargo arriving in Egypt.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: Import CUSCAR generates an EDIFACT customs-manifest file required by NAFEZA for cargo arriving in Egypt. One file is generated per Voyage + Egyptian Port + optional Booking selection from live Booking, Voyage, Vessel, Container and Customer data. Only Import, Load Transshipment or All-leg voyages touching an Egyptian port are offered. Export CUSCAR is a separate screen.

steps.title: Open Cuscar List
steps.desc: Sidebar → EDI → Cuscar List (edi + generate_edi flags).

steps.title: Select Voyage & Port
steps.desc: Pick an eligible Import voyage and the Egyptian manifest port.

steps.title: Generate CUSCAR
steps.desc: Confirmed bookings load for the voyage/port; press Generate.

steps.title: System Validates All Data
steps.desc: Checks containers, vessel, ETA, ACID/tax IDs, exporter country and tare weight.

steps.title: Manifest Saved & Downloaded
outcomes: Valid selection produces a saved .edi file
Any validation failure produces an Excel error report instead

sections.heading: List screen
sections.content: Shows generated CUSCAR records visible when the user generated them or their company appears in line_id. Columns: Ref No, Voyage/Vessel, Port, Shipment Type, BL Count and Created At. BL Count opens bookings grouped by carrier line when cross-company. Actions: Show and Download.

sections.heading: Search filters
items: Voyage / Vessel

sections.heading: Generate form
items: Pick an Import / Load-Transshipment voyage that touches Egypt.
Pick the Egyptian Port for the manifest.
Optionally filter by a specific destination port.
Select confirmed bookings (booking_confirm = 1 or 4). Selecting none includes every matching booking.
Leave Cross enabled (default) to include sibling voyages with the same voyage_no + serial across the company-code group.

sections.heading: Duplicate-generation guard
sections.content: Generation is blocked when the same sibling-voyage pool, port, is_load_port and booking selection already exists. The user is directed to re-download the existing Ref No from the list.

sections.heading: Request-level container checks
items: Every Booking container-detail row must have a selected Container.
Every selected Container must have an Equipment Type.
A failure rejects the whole request before CUSCAR building begins.

sections.heading: Parent / child Booking merge
sections.content: Booking references differing only by leading slashes are treated as one logical shipment. The row with the fewest slashes is the parent; child containers are merged into it so the file contains one CNI consignment per real shipment.

sections.heading: Per-booking validation
items: Vessel Call Sign and IMO Number are required; missing either rejects every booking on that voyage.
An ETA must exist for the relevant Egyptian or leg-arrival port.
Egypt-bound full-container bookings require a 19-digit ACID.
Egypt-bound full-container bookings require a 9-digit Egyptian Importer Tax ID.
Exporter ID is required, alphanumeric and up to 35 characters.
Exporter Country must have a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.
Every Container requires Tare Weight, including empty/transhipment bookings.

sections.heading: Validation failure behaviour
sections.content: If any booking fails per-booking validation, no .edi file is saved. The request returns a CuscarErrorsExport Excel report containing booking reference, vessel/voyage and the exact reason. Generation succeeds only when every selected booking passes.

sections.heading: Cross-company sharing
items: Cross is enabled by default and loads confirmed bookings from sibling voyages sharing voyage_no + serial across companies in the same company-code group.
Every involved company ID is stored in line_id.
Users from any involved sister company can see and re-download the same saved CUSCAR.
List and Show group bookings by carrier line when multiple companies are involved.

sections.heading: What the .edi file contains
items: One EDIFACT CUSCAR D.95B message inside a UNB/UNH…UNT/UNZ envelope.
Header includes sender/receiver, Egypt-time creation timestamp, vessel IMO, call sign, vessel name and voyage transport details.
Direct, transhipment and transit shipments use different transport-stage handling.
FCL containers are declared at message-header level; each booking receives a CNI consignment block with ports, parties and goods.
Goods include container weight, description and detected IMO dangerous-goods classification.
Free text is sanitized to plain ASCII, including conversion of look-alike Cyrillic characters.

sections.heading: CUSCAR record & filename
rows: CUSC + company booking_code + voyage number + per-company running serial from Settings.cuscar_ref_no.
Voyage, port, is_load_port, sorted booking_ids (or null for all), and all involved company IDs in line_id.

sections.heading: Show & re-download
sections.content: Show opens bookings grouped by carrier line and lazy-loads Container details. Download does not replay a stored file: it regenerates the .edi content from current master data using the saved booking selection, so corrections appear in the re-download.

sections.heading: Inbound CUSCAR is a separate workflow
sections.content: A separate implemented but currently unlinked Upload EDI workflow consumes a CUSCAR received from another party and can create Bookings, Containers and an EdiUpload audit record. It validates UNB sender/receiver against the current company. It is not the Generate CUSCAR screen documented here.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Import CUSCAR is a regulatory-compliance generator for Egyptian customs. Its validation report is often the earliest precise signal of missing ACID/tax IDs, vessel IMO/call sign, ETA, customer country or Container tare weight.

modules.title: Export CUSCAR
modules.summary: Generates the EDIFACT CUSCAR D.95B customs manifest required by NAFEZA for cargo leaving Egypt — one file per Voyage + Egyptian load port + chosen BL Drafts.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: Export CUSCAR builds the EDIFACT customs-manifest file required by NAFEZA for cargo leaving Egypt. One file is generated per Voyage + Egyptian Load Port + a chosen set of BL Drafts from live Export BL, Booking and Voyage data. Only voyages whose leg is Export or All, that touch at least one Egyptian port, and that already have at least one BL Draft are offered. Import arrivals are generated on Cuscar List, not here. Both screens write into the same CUSCAR table; Export rows are the ones whose Egyptian port is the load port (is_load_port = 1).

steps.title: Open Export CUSCAR
steps.desc: Sidebar → EDI → Export Cuscar. The list shows this company’s previously generated export files.

steps.title: Generate Export CUSCAR
steps.desc: Pick an Export voyage, the Egyptian load port if there is more than one, and at least one BL Draft (all ticked by default).

steps.title: All BLs Must Pass
steps.desc: Vessel IMO/call sign, ETD, exporter tax ID, assigned containers and tare are validated. Any failure downloads an Excel error report and saves nothing.

steps.title: File Saved
outcomes: A CUSC-EXP- ref is stored and the .edi file downloads
Submit to Nafeza is a separate, stricter step

sections.heading: The list screen
items: Shows only this company’s export CUSCARs (is_load_port = 1), newest first, 30 per page.
Columns: Ref No, Voyage/Vessel, Port (Load), clickable BL Count, Created At, Nafeza badge, Actions.
Nafeza badge: Uploaded (every linked booking Manifest Uploaded), N/M (some uploaded), or a dash (none).
The Vessel/Voyage filter dropdown is filled with eligible voyages, but pressing Filter currently does not narrow the table — voyage_id is posted and ignored.

sections.heading: Generate modal
items: Opened from Generate Export CUSCAR on the list — not a separate full page like Import CUSCAR.
If the voyage has exactly one Egyptian port it is used automatically; otherwise a Load Port dropdown appears.
Every BL Draft starts ticked. At least one must stay ticked — unlike Import, select none = all does not apply.
Each card shows BL ref, booking ref, UCR (green) or No UCR on booking (red), and consignee.
Missing UCR does not block Generate — it only blocks Submit to Nafeza later.

sections.heading: Validation before the file is saved
rows: Voyage, Load Port, and at least one BL Draft.
Meant to block the same company + voyage + load port + BL set. It currently compares new bl_draft_ids against the old record’s booking_ids, so a true duplicate is usually not caught.
Every container line on each selected BL’s booking must already have a real container. Failures return export_cuscar_errors_[Egypt-time].xlsx.
Call Sign and IMO Number must both be filled — failure hits every BL on the voyage.
Voyage Ports must have an ETD for that booking’s load port. Export uses departure, not ETA.
Optional at Generate. If present (and not just 0) it must be exactly 19 digits.
booking.exportal_id, else customer tax card, else BL shipper tax card. Required, exactly 9 digits.
Required on every assigned container. Defaults tried from size + category (20 Dry 2150, 40 Dry 3750, 20 Reefer 2900, 40 Reefer 4560).

sections.heading: Partial success is not written
sections.content: Unlike Import, a partial success (some BLs good, some bad) is not saved. All selected BLs must pass or the whole run stops, no CUSCAR row is created, and the Excel error report is downloaded.

sections.heading: What is written
rows: One EDIFACT CUSCAR D.95B message. Sender = company line code, receiver = NAFEZA.
Egyptian LOAD port (LOC+9) and ETD (DTM+133). Direction EXPORT.
From the BL Draft: shipper NAD+CZ, consignee NAD+CN, notify if present. UCR as RFF+AFM after the shipper.
CUSC-EXP- + company booking_code + voyage number + running Settings.cuscar_ref_no. Import uses CUSC without -EXP-.

sections.heading: Show, re-download and Nafeza
items: Download re-generates the .edi from current BL/booking/vessel/container data using the saved bl_draft_ids — it is not a stored snapshot.
The Show page Re-generate CUSCAR link only sends voyage + load port, so create validation rejects it. Use the list Download button to rebuild the same selection.
Submit to Nafeza (when enabled) re-generates the EDI and POSTs it. Every linked booking must have a valid 19-digit UCR (not blank, not 19 zeroes).
On success the bookings are marked Manifest Uploaded and the list badge flips to Uploaded.
Generate & Download only produces the local .edi file. Submit is the only place on this screen that talks to Nafeza.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Export CUSCAR is the outbound customs manifest for cargo leaving Egypt. Generate is the data-quality gate (vessel IMO/call sign, ETD, exporter tax ID, container assignment, tare). Submit to Nafeza is the compliance gate (every BL must already have a 19-digit UCR). The most common live mistake is generating a file that still has no UCR — it downloads fine and then fails on Submit.

modules.title: Truckers List
modules.summary: Master list of trucking companies that move containers for bookings — feeds CRO trucker assignment, Trucker Guarantees and Trucking Tariffs.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: The master list of trucking companies (truckers) that pull containers in and out of the port/depot for our bookings. A trucker on its own does nothing — it becomes important when it is used elsewhere: assigned as the "CRO trucker" on a booking (printed on the CRO, Gate In and VGM letters), holds a Trucker Guarantee (cash/cheque deposit) against container movements, or has a Trucking Tariff (price list) set against it.

steps.title: Open Truckers List
steps.desc: Sidebar → Trucking → Truckers List (operations + truckers_list flags).

steps.title: Search by Name
steps.desc: Check the trucker is not already registered before adding a new one.

steps.title: Enter Details & Save
steps.desc: Name is required; Phone, Address, Contact Person, Tax No and attachments are optional.

steps.title: System Checks Uniqueness
steps.desc: Phone and Tax No must be unique across every trucker, company-wide.

steps.title: Trucker Ready Everywhere
outcomes: Selectable as CRO trucker, in Trucker Guarantees and Trucking Tariffs
Delete blocked while a guarantee or a booking still uses it

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Optional, max 50 characters. Must be UNIQUE across all truckers. Only digits, spaces and + - ( ) are accepted.
Optional. If filled, must be exactly 9 or 14 digits (Egyptian tax / commercial register format) and UNIQUE across all truckers.
Optional, multiple files. PDF, JPG or PNG only, max 2 MB each. Shown as a paperclip button with a file count in the list.

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: 30 truckers per page, in the order they were created. One search box for Name (partial match). Columns: Name, Tax No, Phone, Address, Contact Person, Attach. The paperclip button opens a pop-up with every attached file (click to open, X to remove immediately). The list is NOT filtered by company — every company sees the same truckers.

sections.heading: Creating & editing rules
rows: This phone number is already registered for another trucker.
The tax number must be either 9 or 14 digits (Egyptian format).
This tax number is already registered.

sections.heading: Edit behaviour
sections.content: On edit, the same rules apply (the uniqueness check ignores the trucker being edited). New files are ADDED to the existing ones — uploading does not replace old attachments. Old files are removed one by one with their X button.

sections.heading: Delete rules
rows: Cannot delete this trucker because it has a related trucker guarantee.
Trucker is the CRO trucker on any booking
Cannot delete this trucker because it has related booking records.

sections.heading: Bulk upload (Excel)
items: "Upload" accepts .xlsx / .xls / .csv (max 2 MB). The first row must be the headers: name, tax_no, phone, address, contact_person.
Each row is checked with the same rules as the form: name required, phone and tax number not already used, tax number 9 or 14 digits.
Valid rows become new truckers, stamped with the uploader's company.

sections.heading: How this feeds other modules
rows: The trucker list shown on a booking is ALL truckers. If the trucker is changed, the system re-checks the Trucker Guarantee holds for every container on that booking that already has a WTOR / GIMT / GOMT / GIFU movement, so the held amount moves to the new trucker's guarantee.

CRO letter uses the trucker chosen when printing (falls back to the booking's CRO trucker if none found for this company). Gate In letter prints the booking's CRO trucker name, or "-". VGM letter prints the booking's CRO trucker name only.

Creating WTOR movements from a booking writes the trucker's name into the movement Remarks. Movement Control's trucker filter only lists truckers actually used on this company's bookings. Movement Excel exports include the booking's CRO trucker name.
Both screens pick the trucker from this list.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: The trucker is the link between a booking, the containers leaving the port, and the money we hold as guarantee. If the same trucker is registered twice under slightly different names, guarantees and bookings get split across two records, so one copy shows no guarantee balance while the other holds the containers. Always search by name before adding a new trucker.

modules.title: Trucker Guarantees
modules.summary: Records the financial guarantee a trucker leaves before taking our containers, and tracks — live — how much of it is still free.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: A trucker who takes our containers out of the port must leave a financial guarantee (a guarantee letter, and optionally a cheque). This screen records that guarantee and shows, live, how much of it is still free. Every container the trucker currently has out is "held" against the guarantee at the price of its Equipment Type. When the container comes back, the hold is released and the money becomes available again. Holds are NOT entered by the user — they are created and released automatically from Movement Control and Booking.

steps.title: Prep Trucker & Prices
steps.desc: Trucker must already exist; every Equipment Type needs a Price (Container Control → Equipment Types).

steps.title: Pick Trucker & Dates
steps.desc: Trucking → Trucker Guarantees → Add New. One guarantee per trucker.

steps.title: Save & Preview Balance
steps.desc: Available Balance previews amount minus containers this trucker already has out.

steps.title: System Holds & Releases Automatically
steps.desc: WTOR / GOMT hold the container price; GIMT / GIFU / STRP / RCVE release it.

steps.title: Guarantee Protects Bookings
outcomes: Assignment is blocked/warned when balance is short
Auto-set to Inactive 2 days before Valid To

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Required. ONE guarantee per trucker only. Locked (cannot be changed) once any container is held against it.
Required dates. Valid To must be on or after Valid From.
Required, 0 or more. The main guarantee value.
Optional, 0 or more. Only counted while Status is "Extend" — ignored in any other status.
Never typed. Always calculated. Can be NEGATIVE — that shows how far the trucker is over the limit.
Active / Hold / Extend / Inactive. Locked while held containers are using part of the cheque.

sections.heading: Status meanings
rows: Normal. Trucker can be assigned to bookings.
Same as Active, plus the Cheque Amount is added to the total.
Trucker is hidden from the booking trucker list.
Trucker is hidden from the booking trucker list. Shown with a red badge and warning icon. Set automatically near expiry.

sections.heading: Search filters
items: Trucker
Status

sections.heading: Listing & export
sections.content: 30 per page, newest first. Columns: Trucker, Valid From, Valid To, Total Amount (letter + cheque if Extend), Available Balance, Status badge (Active = green, Hold = yellow, Extend = blue, Inactive = red). "Export" downloads TruckerGuarantees.xlsx with the same filters and columns. If nothing matches: "No Trucker Guarantees found."

sections.heading: Creating & editing rules
rows: This trucker already has a guarantee.

sections.heading: Edit locks
items: On SAVE (create or edit) the system re-scans every container ever put on a booking of this trucker and rebuilds the held list, so containers that went out BEFORE the guarantee existed are picked up immediately.
Trucker cannot be changed once containers are held.

Status cannot be changed while Status is Extend AND the held containers exceed the letter amount (they are using the cheque). The form shows: "Locked — the cheque is currently drawn on by held containers."

sections.heading: Delete rule
sections.content: DELETE is blocked when containers are still held: "Cannot delete this guarantee because it has containers currently held against it."

sections.heading: How the balance is calculated
items: Total = Letter Amount (+ Cheque Amount, only while Status = Extend).
Held = sum of prices of containers currently held.
Available Balance = Total − Held.
Container price = the Price of the container's Equipment Type. The letter amount is used first; the cheque is only "used" by the part of Held that is above the letter amount.

sections.heading: When a container is held or released
Hold / release rules
items: Checked every time a movement is created, edited, deleted or restored for that container (and when a guarantee is saved).
Only movements linked to a booking that HAS a CRO trucker count. The guarantee used is the one of that booking's trucker — if the trucker has no guarantee, nothing is held.
If the booking's trucker is changed, the hold moves to the new trucker's guarantee.
If the data shows a container open on two bookings, the most recent one wins.

sections.heading: SOC containers — never deducted from the balance
items: SOC (Shipper-Owned) containers belong to the shipper, not to us, so the trucker's guarantee does not cover them.

Assigning the trucker: SOC containers are left out of the booking cost, so they never cause an "Insufficient Balance" warning, and a missing Equipment Type price on an SOC container does not block the assignment.
Gate out (WTOR / GOMT): nothing is held for an SOC container, and the Available Balance does not change.
Mixed booking (SOC + COC): only the COC containers are held and deducted.

A container counts as SOC when its SOC / COC field in Container List is "SOC" (or, before a container number is attached, when the booking line is marked SOC). If a container is changed to SOC after it was held, the hold is NOT released immediately — it is released the next time that container has a movement added/edited/deleted, or when the trucker's guarantee is saved.

sections.heading: How this feeds Booking (trucker assignment) — MLH only
items: Truckers whose guarantee is Hold, Inactive or past Valid To are removed from the picker (the booking's current trucker always stays).
If any non-SOC container type on the booking has no Equipment Type Price, assignment is blocked with "Equipment Type Price Missing".
Booking cost = sum of Equipment Type price × quantity of the booking's non-SOC containers.

Available ≥ cost → selectable, no warning. Available < cost → "Insufficient Balance" popup with shortfall and projected balance (user can confirm). No valid guarantee → "No Trucker Guarantee" popup to create one on the spot (dates only, amount 0, status Active).

sections.heading: Equipment Type price lock
sections.content: This part applies to multi-line (MLH) companies only — other companies see a plain list of all truckers with no balance checks. The Price of an Equipment Type becomes read-only once any container of that type is held against a guarantee.

sections.heading: Automatic expiry
sections.content: Every day at 21:00 the system sets to Inactive every guarantee whose Valid To is within the next 2 days or already passed (whatever its status, including Extend). It stays Inactive even if someone later extends Valid To — the user must also change the Status back.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: This is the company's protection against a trucker keeping or losing containers. Wrong or missing data here fails silently: no Equipment Type price means containers are held at 0; a missing guarantee means nothing is held at all; an expired guarantee makes the trucker vanish from bookings. When a balance looks wrong, check the container movements (WTOR/GOMT out, GIMT/GIFU back) and the booking's trucker — not this form.

modules.title: Trucking Tariffs

sections.content: The price list agreed with a trucker for moving containers between two Egyptian terminals/depots, for a period of time. For every container size (20ft / 40ft) it stores three charges — Trucking, Lift On and Lift Off — each with a COST (what the trucker charges us) and a SELLING RATE (what we charge the customer). Its only consumer is Trucking Orders: when an order is created, the selling rates are copied from the chosen tariff.

sections.heading: Listing
sections.content: Only the user's company tariffs, 30 per page, newest first. No search filters. Columns: Reference, Trucker, From Terminal, To Terminal, Validity, Container Sizes. A details pop-up shows cost and selling rate per size and charge type.

sections.content: Trucking Orders take their prices straight from here, so a wrong selling rate or a wrong validity period goes directly onto every new order. Keep one tariff per trucker and route per period, renew it with new dates instead of editing old ones, and never delete a tariff that already has orders.

modules.title: Trucking Orders
modules.summary: A job order given to a trucker, priced from a Trucking Tariff — a stand-alone record with no booking, invoice or cost link.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: A Trucking Order (job order) records a trucking job given to a trucker: which tariff it is priced on, the issue date, the container sizes, and the charge lines (charge type × size × quantity × selling rate = total). Prices are copied from the chosen Trucking Tariff when the order is prepared. The order is a stand-alone record: it is not linked to a booking, and it does not create an invoice or a cost.

steps.title: Confirm Tariff Exists
steps.desc: A valid Trucking Tariff must already exist for the trucker.

steps.title: Open Trucking Orders
steps.desc: Trucking → Trucking Orders → Add New.

steps.desc: Charge lines auto-fill from the tariff; adjust quantities; set the Issue Date.

steps.title: Job Order Saved

rows: Never typed. "serial/year", e.g. 15/2026. The serial restarts at 1 every calendar year, per company. Kept unchanged on edit.

sections.heading: How lines are filled
sections.content: Every time the Tariff or the Container Sizes change, the lines are REPLACED with the tariff's selling rates (one line per charge type per size, quantity 1). Manual changes are lost at that point — pick tariff and sizes first, then edit quantities. If the tariff has no rates for those sizes: "No charges found for the selected tariff and container sizes." sections.heading: Creating & editing rules
rows: Issue date must be on or after the tariff validity from date (YYYY-MM-DD).

Duplicate charge type: [Charge] for the same equipment [size]ft already exists.

sections.content: On edit, all lines are deleted and re-saved from the form.

sections.heading: Deleting
sections.content: Asks for confirmation and deletes the order and its lines. No checks. Orders are also deleted automatically if their Tariff is deleted.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: The Trucking Order is the written record of what was agreed with the trucker for a job and at what price. Because it copies prices from the tariff at the moment of creation, the tariff must be correct and valid on the issue date BEFORE the order is made. The most common problem is an expired tariff: the issue date is rejected until a new tariff period is created.

modules.title: Invoice Period
modules.summary: Invoice Period is a read / report screen across every Switch Line that shares the same companies.code as the company you are on.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: Invoice Period is a read / report screen across every Switch Line that shares the same companies.code as the company you are on. It is not where invoices are created, edited, confirmed or deleted — that stays on Invoice List (or Yard List). Here you: - filter a period (or a BL, invoice number, voyage or type), - see invoices from all sibling lines in one table, - read currency totals for that filtered set, - Print All (one merged PDF), Download ZIP, or Export Excel. Accountants use it for "everything under this company code this month" without switching line by line. Credit notes (type C) never appear here.

steps.title: Open Invoice Period
steps.desc: Sidebar → Accounting → Invoice Period (invoice_gates flag).

steps.title: Search & Locate
steps.desc: Filter or search the list to find the right record.

steps.title: Enter Details & Save
steps.desc: 1. Open Accounting

steps.title: System Validates
steps.desc: Required fields, guards, and business rules are enforced before save.

steps.title: Ready in System
outcomes: Invoice Period. 2. The page shows filters only. The table stays empty until you apply at least one filter and click Filter (an info banner explains this). 3.…
Downstream screens can consume the updated data

sections.heading: What This Screen Shows
sections.content: Column / area Meaning Line companies.code and line_code of the invoice's company (so you can see which sibling line owns the row). Invoice No The invoice number on that line. Customer / Tax NO Bill-to customer and tax card number. Bl No Import booking ref or export B/L ref linked to the invoice. Voyage / Vessel From the booking or B/L (second voyage when the booking is marked transhipment). Date Invoice date (this is what the date filters use). Type Shipping invoice type, or "Yard …" when on a yard line. payment kind From the linked booking / B/L booking. Currency amounts USD, EGP and any other active currencies. Only the invoice's own currency cell is filled on the row. Invoice Status Draft / Ready To Confirm / Confirm / Void. Payment Status Paid / Partially Paid / UnPaid from the invoice and its valid receipts. Receipts Receipt numbers already applied. Actions Print PDF for that row; optional QB sync. INCLUDED Confirmed and draft invoices (and other non-credit types) for every company id in the same companies.code group as the user. EXCLUDED Credit notes (type C). Invoices on a different company code (e.g. MLHC when you are on MLHE). Yard invoices while you are on a shipping line, and shipping invoices while you are on a yard line.

sections.heading: Company Scope & Yard Rules
items: WHOSE INVOICES YOU SEE Scope follows Company::idsForCompanyCombined for the signed-in company:
1) If companies.code is set → every company row with that same code. 2) Else → every company row with the same agency_code.
With the usual MLH setup (code is set):
On an MLHE line → only MLHE sibling lines On an MLHC line → only MLHC sibling lines On YARD (code YARD, e.g. YRDALX + YRDSOK) → yard invoices for those yard lines only
Do not expect MLHE and MLHC together on this screen. Invoice Period groups by company CODE, not by the whole agency.
SHIPPING LINE (booking_code is not YRD) Rows come from the invoices table for the code group. Totals split by currency (USD / EGP / other active currencies).
YARD LINE (booking_code = YRD) Switch Line to a yard company first. Rows come from yard_invoices for every yard line under the same code. Shipping invoices are not mixed in.
BL filters look up B/Ls and bookings on the paired shipping companies:
YRDALX → companies with code MLHE YRDSOK → companies with code MLHC
Choosing shipping-only invoice types (Storage, Detention, Power, …) returns no yard rows. Yard keeps invoice / debit style types only.

sections.heading: Listing, Search, Totals & Print
sections.content: LIST - Empty until at least one filter is applied. - 30 per page, newest date then id first. - Header shows result count and currency totals for the whole filtered set (all pages). FILTERS (any one is enough to load the table) Invoices From / To Date range on invoice date. If From is set and To is empty, To defaults to today. From cannot be after To; To cannot be after today on the form. Invoice Status Draft / Ready To Confirm / Confirm / All. Voyages Voyages from the same company-code group. Selecting a voyage also allows BL search across that group. Invoice Type Multi-select (plus Storage / Detention / Power / Customized / Transit shortcuts). Shipment Type All / Import / Transhipment / Export (options depend on whether the user may see import and/or export invoices). Bl Number Multi; type at least 3 characters to search Import or Export refs across the company code. Invoice No Type at least 3 characters to search; filter matches that number across the company code. QB Sync Status Only when QuickBooks is enabled (Synced / Failed / Not Synced). TOTALS Shipping: for type "invoice", charge lines use the VAT-inclusive fields (egp_vat / usd_vat); other types use total_egy / total_amount. Amounts land in EGP, USD or another active currency column by the invoice currency. Yard: EGP-oriented (per line max of egp_vat and total_egy for type invoice; otherwise total_egy). USD / other currency columns stay empty on yard rows. Charge lines on an invoice are snapshots. Changing the master charge catalogue does not rewrite old invoices. PRINT ALL / DOWNLOAD ZIP / EXPORT All three use the current filters plus company_combined=1. Print All One merged PDF of the filtered set. Download ZIP One ZIP of individual PDFs. Export Excel — All Details, or Inv. Breakdown. Up to 20 invoices: Print All / ZIP run immediately. More than 20: background job with a progress card, then download (same idea as receipt and credit-note ZIP). Excel always runs in the background. Toolbar buttons stay disabled until a filter is applied.

sections.heading: How This Feeds Other Modules
items: INVOICE LIST / YARD LIST Unchanged. Day-to-day create / edit / confirm still happens there, one Switch Line at a time. Invoice Period only reads the same invoice (or yard invoice) rows across the code group.
RECEIPTS & PAYMENT STATUS Receipt numbers and Paid / Partially Paid / UnPaid on each row come from the invoice's existing receipts. Nothing on this screen creates or edits a receipt.
QUICKBOOKS When enabled, confirmed rows can be synced or resynced from the Actions column, same idea as Invoice List. The optional QB Sync Status filter only limits which rows appear.

PRINT / EXCEL JOBS Merged PDF, ZIP and Excel jobs are the shared invoice export / PDF pipeline with company_combined=1 (yard uses the yard variants when you are on a yard line). Filters on the URL are what the job prints or exports.
OTHER ACCOUNTING SCREENS Credit Note, Cost and single-line Invoice List are separate. This screen does not post, credit or reverse anything.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Without Invoice Period, period close and management reporting for a multi-line company code means switching line by line and pasting lists together. Totals then disagree because each list only saw one company_id. The hard rule that keeps the numbers trustworthy is the company CODE boundary: MLHE and MLHC (and their yards) stay separate on purpose. If an invoice is "missing", first check whether you are on the right Switch Line family, whether a filter is applied, and whether the document is a credit note — those three explain most empty or short results. Treat this screen as the period lens, not the working desk. Fix data on Invoice List or Yard List; come back here to see the combined picture and to print or export the filtered set.

modules.title: Credit Note
modules.summary: Refunds part or all of a confirmed Invoice or Debit Note — lowers what is left to collect, can credit the customer balance, and releases Storage / Detention / Power so they can be re-issued.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: A Credit Note reduces (refunds) what a customer owes. It is usually issued against a confirmed Invoice or Debit Note and gives back part or all of its charges; it can also be issued on its own for a customer. The credit note is saved in the invoice table as type C. It lowers the remaining amount to collect on the original invoice, can add the amount to the customer’s credit balance when that invoice was already paid, and releases storage / detention / power invoices so they can be recalculated and re-issued. Yard companies see Yard Credit Note instead — a separate screen, not covered here.

steps.title: Add Credit Note

steps.title: Header Fills In
steps.desc: Customer, booking / B/L, ports, voyage, currency, exchange rate, VAT and the refundable charges fill automatically.

steps.title: Adjust Refund Amounts

steps.title: Remaining Amounts Checked

items: If a number is typed, it is used as is.

MLH companies: generated from the MLH serial counters shared by the company group. CNINV = credit note on an invoice (5-digit). CNSC = credit note on a debit note (6-digit). Digit 1 = import, 2 = export (3 / 4 for MLHC).

sections.content: A credit note cannot be edited once a newer credit note was created on the same invoice charges. The list shows a lock icon instead of Edit. Credit notes cannot be deleted from this screen. Correct mistakes with a new credit note instead of editing an older one.

items: The invoice, booking and B/L stay as they were.
Charge lines are replaced and checked again. Each line may go up to its remaining amount plus what this credit note already had.
VAT % and quantity are updated.
Customer, date, currency, exchange rate and notes are not updated by Edit.

sections.heading: How this feeds other modules
items: Remaining amount to collect on an invoice is its total minus its confirmed credit notes. Receipts use that remaining amount. Fully credited invoices are shown in red.

If the parent invoice is already paid, the credited amount (after VAT) is added to the customer’s credit balance in the note’s currency. Credit notes on unpaid invoices, or without an invoice, do not change the balance.

A credited Storage / Detention / Power invoice (or extension) is ignored when checking whether such an invoice already exists, when the CRO letter reads the last storage invoice, and when booking calculations look for existing invoices.
A booking is no longer flagged as having an unpaid invoice when that invoice is fully credited.
QuickBooks: green Sync queues the credit note. The Web Connector must then run to finish.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Credit notes directly change what customers owe, their credit balance, and whether storage / detention can be invoiced again. Always create them from the original invoice so the system can check the remaining amounts. Once a newer credit note exists on the same charges, older ones are frozen.

modules.title: Cost (Vendor Bills)
modules.summary: Vendor bills for what the company owes a supplier — depot storage, THC, ocean freight, trucking, DA. Totals are calculated from charge lines and container rates, not stored.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: This is where the company records what it owes a supplier — depot storage, terminal THC, ocean freight, trucking, DA and the rest. It is a vendor bill, not a customer invoice. The list button says Add Vendor Bill for that reason. A Cost has a header (who billed us, which bill number, which dates, which currency) and one or more charge lines taken from that supplier’s charge-item catalogue. Each line can then be broken down onto real BLs, bookings or container numbers, with a rate per box and, for storage, a quantity of days. Nothing here posts to QuickBooks. The QB columns on a charge line are labels copied from the supplier catalogue so accountants can recognise the item later.

sections.heading: Access
rows: Cost-List, Cost-Create, Cost-Show, Cost-Edit, Cost-Delete, plus Cost-Store on save
Soft-delete. The bill, charge lines, container links and attachment file are removed, but the row stays in the table.
